title: Reduce routing hotpaths and standardize fallback contracts
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
We will reduce contention in the smart routing hot path by extracting decision-heavy logic out of the per-request fast path and introducing a thin runtime contract for fallback behaviors. Goals are to: 1) remove allocations and locks from the hot path, 2) make fallback semantics deterministic across regions, and 3) expose a compact, versioned fallback contract so Dedicated/Private builds can opt-in to optimized implementations.

Scope:
- Refactor: split policy evaluation into (a) pre-evaluated route hints computed asynchronously and cached, and (b) a minimal hot-path selector that only inspects compact hints.
- Fallback contract: define a small interface (fallback_code, max_tries, shard_affinity_hint) and replace ad-hoc JSON blobs and region-specific branching with a schema-validated structure.
- Regional cleanup: unify region affinity metadata and remove duplicate region override checks scattered across the codebase.
- Performance cleanup: remove mutexes around decision cache, replace with lock-free ring buffer for short-lived ephemeral state, and reduce heap allocations by pooling small structs.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Full migration of legacy policy DSL (will be follow-up),
- UI/Console changes (metrics and rollout views are covered in separate ticket).

Success criteria:
- 20-40% reduction in p99 routing latency for small requests in our synthetic microbench (>10k qps),
- No increase in error rate in the canary region over 48h,
- All unit and integration tests pass and CI latency remains stable,
- Fallback contract defined and documented in Confluence + schema validated in CI.

Design notes / trade-offs considered:
- Option A (aggressive): inline decision hints into request proto to eliminate cache lookups in hotpath. Pros: minimal branching, lowest latency. Cons: larger wire and versioning complexity.
- Option B (chosen): keep hints in local in-memory cache with TTL and use a tiny descriptor copied into the request context on admission. This keeps wire unchanged while drastically reducing decision cost on hotpath.
- Chosen lock-free ring-buffer uses sequence counters and single-writer semantics to avoid ABA; trade-off is slightly more complex reasoning but lower contention under 1000s of cores.

Migration plan:
1) Add fallback contract schema and validate it in tests (non-breaking).
2) Implement hint pre-evaluator as background worker and populate cache; initial mode: "read-through" so existing paths still work.
3) Introduce hotpath selector that reads compact hint; run canary in a single region (eu-west-1).
4) Monitor for 72 hours, collect p95/p99, error rates, and CPU.
5) Gradually expand to other regions and enable aggressive eviction.

Rollout safety:
- Feature gate behind runtime-2.3 flag "compact-routing-hotpath".
- Automatic rollback on error spikes (>2x baseline error rate) or latency regression (>20% p99 increase).

Telemetry and tests:
- Add metrics: routing.hint_cache.hit_rate, routing.selector.latency_ms.{p50,p95,p99}, routing.fallback.invocations, routing.fallback.path_distribution.
- Unit tests for fallback schema validation and selector edge cases.
- Integration test that simulates region failover and asserts deterministic fallback.

Risks:
- Subtle incompatibility between legacy fallback blobs and the new contract; mitigated by backward-compatible parser for one release.
- Memory pressure from caching hints at very high cardinality customers; mitigation: size-based LRU and per-customer cap.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Compact+Routing+Hotpath+RFC
- Design doc (in repo): docs/routing/compact-hotpath.md
- Draft fallback contract schema: tools/schemas/fallback_contract_v1.json
